A narrow surface trough is moving across the Marianas this evening, 
however, this trough is expected to bring a slight uptick in shower 
potential from 10 percent to 20 percent. At this time an over-
achieving shower is not out of the question, but is unlikely. 
Isolated showers are expected through the remainder of the week. 
Enjoy the sunny days, but try to start conserving water as we look to
be moving into the dry season.

Marine...
The marine forecast remains relatively unchanged for the short term,
with combined seas of 5 to 6 feet tonight and Monday. Seas then look
to build a foot or so beginning Monday night. The biggest change in 
the marine forecast is the increase in the northwest swell that is 
expected to move in from Typhoon Cempaka (31W). This will push a 
northwest swell into the region by the middle of next week that 
looks to become the dominant swell. With an expected long period, 
this could result in another high risk of rip currents and hazardous 
surf along west and north facing reefs.

Tropical Systems...
Cempaka (31W) was upgraded to a typhoon at 1:00 PM ChST. Cempaka was
located about 530 miles west-northwest of Agrihan near 21.6N 138.1E,
moving west at 14 mph. Maximum sustained winds have increased to 75 
mph. Cempaka is expected to maintain its current heading with a 
decrease in forward speed over the next couple of days, then turn 
toward the northeast around Tuesday. Cempaka is expected to 
strengthen over the next couple of days. Cempaka no longer poses a 
direct threat to any islands in the Marianas or Micronesia as it 
progresses.

For more information on TY Cempaka, see bulletins issued by the 
Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW and by the 
National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
The main item of interest is a broad/weak circulation located near
Kosrae, that's located along a Near-Equatorial Trough. This low 
looks to remain quasi-stationary the next few days as it slowly 
weakens. The showers have remained east of Kosrae this afternoon, as
surface convergence remains weak there. This limits rainfall 
potential to an extent, so rainfall coverage and probabilities were 
decreased over the next 48 hours, given the expected dissipation of 
the circulation.

Farther northwest and northeast, Pohnpei remains removed from the
better surface convergence, so look for just isolated showers there
for at least the next few days. Meanwhile, at Majuro, the "strongest"
convergence is located to your north and west. We currently have just
isolated shower coverage there for the next 48 hours, but satellite
trends will need to be monitored for potential increasing convective
coverage in the short term (next 48 hours), as the better convective
coverage is not too far away, and am a little suspect of the model
forecasts showing a decreasing convective signature.

Also at Majuro, the Pikareej buoy is showing a northeast swell
between 5 and 6 feet at 11 seconds. Although this remains below
advisory levels, we inserted an elevated headline in the forecast
through Monday, and trends will continue to be monitored. Otherwise,
light to gentle winds will prevail area-wide. Seas of 4 to 6 feet 
are expected the next few days at Pohnpei and Kosrae, with Majuro 
remaining in the 5 to 8 foot range (highest north and east of the 
atolls), before a decrease is expected.

Western Micronesia...
Unsettled weather continues over far western Micronesia this 
afternoon. Himawari visible satellite shows numerous showers and 
isolated thunderstorms across the Republic of Palau and western Yap
State, associated with a broad trough that extends south to 
southwest across the area into a buffer circulation over the far 
outer islands of Indonesia. Far to the east, Chuuk is in a drier 
northeast trade regime with isolated showers moving through the area,
beneath swaths of upper-level cloud debris.

Model and satellite trends point to a build-up of showers and
thunderstorms over Yap this evening, as numerous showers and 
isolated thunderstorms continue for Palau overnight. Precipitable
water values range 2.6 to 3.0 inches just east of Palau, and 2.4 to
2.6 inches east of Yap, associated with deeper moisture and
convection along the trough axis. Showers will diminish through
Monday morning as the trough shifts northwestward and convergence 
into its northern periphery begins to decrease. So, low-end 
scattered showers (30 percent chance) were maintained for Yap and 
Palau through the morning, decreasing to isolated showers Monday 
afternoon. Meanwhile, showers are expected to increase near Chuuk 
Monday afternoon as the broad monsoon-like trough to its south, and 
associated convergence, shift northward. Then, a drier pattern will 
resume for Chuuk and Yap through the remainder of the week. For 
Palau, periods of scattered showers are anticipated through at least
